raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Companion to [vllm-project/flash-attention#213](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/213). That PR syncs the 72 Dao-AILab commits from `ce088ab9` through `54b044c8`, with FA3 (`hopper/`) frozen.

**Do not merge** until #213 lands. `GIT_REPOSITORY` temporarily points at `MatthewBonanni/flash-attention`, and `GIT_TAG` pins the #213 head `98da179d5dc5868c4515569dd883d52553d09d37`, so vLLM CI can build and test the candidate. Once #213 lands, this PR will switch back to `vllm-project/flash-attention` and the merged SHA.

## Changes

- `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake`: repository and `GIT_TAG` point at the candidate (temporary).
- `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py`: upstream's `_flash_attn_fwd` now returns 5 values (it adds `o_lo`), so the FA4 call unpacks `out, softmax_lse, _, _, _`.

- Remove vLLM's FA4 hd256 special-casing. It existed for the fork's dedicated hd256 kernel; upstream's unified forward serves head_size=256 without those restrictions.
  - `fa_utils.py`: drop `FA4_HD256_PAGE_SIZE`, `uses_fa4_hd256_kernel`, `_fa4_hd256_fallback_reason`, and the `supports_fa4_hd256` / `requires_softcap` / `kv_cache_block_size` parameters. hd256 no longer falls back to FA2 for sinks, softcap, quantized KV, block sizes that are not a multiple of 128, mm_prefix, R-SWA, DCP, or windowed encoders.
  - `flash_attn.py`: drop the 128-token block-size advertisement, page-aligned `max_seqlen_k`, block-table trimming, and the forced `num_splits=1`. hd256 now uses the default block size (16), and FA4 warmup also compiles the split variant.
  - Callers that never opted in (`mm_encoder_attention`, MLA prefill, TurboQuant/UltraQuant prefill) also resolve FA4 instead of FA2 for 256/256 on Blackwell.
  - `sparse_mla_attention.py`, `triton_flash_attn.py`, `flash_attn_diffkv.py`, `docs/design/attention_backends.md`: remove the hd256 leftovers.
- Tests: delete the four hd256 selector tests; `test_fa4_hd256_paged_call_shape` becomes `test_fa4_hd256_varlen_with_paged_kv` (block 16/128, softcap, sliding window, `num_splits` 1/4, unaligned `max_seqlen_k`, wide block table); `test_mm_prefix_kv_cache_path` adds head_size=256.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn_interface.py`: the mocked `_flash_attn_fwd` returns 5 values, matching upstream.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: **widens the bf16 tolerance for `masked_mha_chunked_context` from `rtol=0.01` to `rtol=0.02`** (see the note below).

## Note: sparse MLA chunked-context tolerance

`test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness[*-masked_mha_chunked_context]` is flaky across seeds on `main` as well. The test fixes `torch.manual_seed(42)`, and the new hd256 kernel happens to fail at that seed.

- **Cause:** the chunked-context path rounds the running context partial to bf16 at every chunk merge, and again in the final suffix merge. With outputs around 128, `rtol=atol=0.01` allows only about 1.3 bf16 ULP. Keeping the running partial in fp32 makes the case pass, which isolates the error to these extra roundings rather than the kernel.
- **Seed sweep:** `torch.manual_seed` patched across seeds 0–299, on B300. "Old" is `main` with stock FA4 (the dedicated hd256 kernel); "new" is this PR with #213.

| shape | kernel | seeds failing at rtol 0.01 | at 0.015 | at 0.02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| deepseek 192/128 | old / new | 21 / 21 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| glm5 256/256 | old / new | 5 / 10 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| glm53 256/256 (NoPE) | old / new | 1 / 6 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

- **New vs old kernel:** the new hd256 kernel exceeds 1 ULP on more seeds than the old dedicated kernel, at about the same rate as FA4's standard kernel on deepseek. The maximum error is the same 1.5 for both, and without chunked context both stay within 1 ULP.
- **Chosen tolerance:** `rtol=0.02` keeps at least 1.06 of margin on every seed. A follow-up could keep the running partial in fp32 instead. That would roughly double the partial buffer's memory and changes shared MLA code, so it is not done here.

## Validation

vLLM `main` plus this branch, precompiled install. `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/cute` was replaced with #213's `flash_attn/cute`, with imports rewritten as the CMake install does. Environment: torch 2.11.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn.py tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_quant_output.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_rel_attention.py tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_warmup.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_cascade_flash_attn.py
```

- **H100 80GB HBM3:** 1002 passed, 68 failed, 794 skipped. All 68 failures are `fa_version=3` cases of `test_varlen_with_paged_kv`, mostly with FP8 Q. They run the unchanged FA3 binary from the precompiled wheel, which this sync does not touch.
- **B300 SXM6 AC:** 908 passed, 1 failed, 955 skipped. The failure is `test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness[glm53_flash_nope_hd256_v256-auto-masked_mha_chunked_context]`. It passes with the stock FA4. One element out of 8,388,608 differs by 1.5 at magnitude ~128 (1.17% relative, against `rtol=atol=0.01`), about 1.5 bf16 ULP.
  - This is the hd256 forward, which moved from the fork's dedicated kernel to upstream's unified one.
  - Measured directly against an fp32 reference, the unified kernel's LSE error is 3–24× lower than the dedicated kernel's. Output error is at bf16 rounding level for both: max relative 1.6e-3 vs 1.2e-3, where bf16 half-ULP is 3.9e-3.
  - So the tolerance in this test is right at the edge.
- **hd256 perf on B300 (`benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`, FLASH_ATTN, block size 128):** compared with fork `main`'s dedicated hd256 kernel, the unified kernel is faster in all 39 cases. Prefill is 1.03–1.42× and decode/mixed is 1.5–9.3×, even with `num_splits=1`. With SplitKV enabled (this PR), small decode batches gain further (`8q1s4k`: 4.8× vs 2.5× at 16/2 heads; 6.0× vs 4.7× at 32/4). One case is slightly worse: `16q4s4k` at 32/4, 5.2× vs 6.2×. Full table in [vllm-project/flash-attention#213](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/213).

**hd256 removal validation (B300, vLLM branch head, precompiled install + #213 FA4 overlay).**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn.py -k fa4_hd256
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_jit_warmup_migration.py tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_quant_output.py
```

- 64 passed; 695 passed, 1 failed (the same `glm53…hd256…chunked_context` single-element miss described above; with the widened tolerance, all 12 `test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness` cases pass). `test_mm_prefix_kv_cache_path[sliding_256]` passes.
- Direct FA4 probes, max abs error vs fp32 reference, hd256 vs hd128 in the same 2–4e-3 range: pages 16–256, unaligned lengths, wide block tables, sinks, softcap, sliding window, splits, unpaged windowed encoder; FP8 Q/K/V with descales 1.45–1.55e-2 (hd128: 1.33–1.72e-2).
- Perf tradeoff: hd256 now defaults to block 16 instead of 128. On B300, block 128 is 1.19–1.47× faster for hd256 prefill/extend and 1.0–1.3× for decode (hd128 sees 1.02–1.25×), since FA4 uses TMA paged KV only when the page equals the 128-token tile. A follow-up PR will prefer 128-token blocks for FA4 in general rather than special-casing hd256.

The full FA2 C++ build is left to CI on this PR.

nodes.body:
### Blocker: Gemma 4 does not start on Hopper

On one H200, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic` with this PR fails in `kernel_warmup`:

```
File ".../vllm_flash_attn/cute/interface.py", line 823, in _flash_attn_fwd
    validate_output_layout(out, "out", align_bytes=out_align_bytes)
AssertionError: out must have aligned strides and a contiguous last dimension
EngineCore failed to start.
```

FA#213 now requires a 32-byte aligned `out` at `head_dim_v == 512`. `FA4DenseAttentionKernel.get_warmup_keys` compiles SM90 hd512 keys through vLLM's own `compile_flash_attn_varlen_func_from_specs` in `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py`, which builds `out` with the default 16-byte alignment. The FA-side fix does not help, because this wrapper builds its own spec. With only the FA fix, the engine still fails with the same assertion.

The fix is the same line in vLLM's wrapper. It is on [`pr65203-review-fixes`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/tree/pr65203-review-fixes) as one commit, [`fa116c71b`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/fa116c71b2393ee48a4ebc5d0810dfe58a9a1f67), on top of `d203078a1`:

```diff
     out = _make_compile_only_tensor_spec(
         (*q_shape[:-1], v_shape[-1]),
         q_dtype,
+        assumed_align=32 if v_shape[-1] == 512 else 16,
     )
```

On the H200 with this fix, the 5 FA4 warmup keys compile in 10.4 s and GSM8K (5-shot) is 0.6475 flexible / 0.6346 strict. The base (vLLM `28dd9c36`, FA `9ed6b129`) warms up in 14 s and scores 0.6467 / 0.6338.

### Known slowdown: Gemma 2 under forced FLASH_ATTN

Before this PR, hd256 with softcap (Gemma 2, `attn_logit_softcapping=50`) fell back to FA2 on SM100. Now it runs on FA4. Accuracy is unchanged (GSM8K 0.831 against 0.829), but FA4's softcap path is slower. On B300, FLASH_ATTN forced, same server flags, interleaved arms, one GSM8K pass (1319 questions, concurrency 256) takes:

| Arm | Wall time per pass (s) |
|---|---|
| FA4 with softcap (this PR) | 37.8, 37.5, 31.0, 32.9 |
| FA2 (`flash_attn_version=2`) | 21.3, 19.9, 23.5, 20.5 |
| FA4, softcap removed by hf override (timing only) | 12.2, 10.5 |

That is about 1.5x slower than FA2. No FA4 run logged a runtime JIT compile, so this is steady state. Block 128 does not recover it (41.9 s). B300 picks FlashInfer for Gemma 2 by default, so only users who force FLASH_ATTN see this. I am not asking for a change here; it may be worth a line in the description.

### Minor: validation env

The perf numbers reproduce under vLLM's own pins (cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11), which this PR keeps. The env in the description (4.8.1 / 0.1.15.post2) cannot run `vllm serve`: after CUDA-graph capture, the JIT monitor imports tilelang 0.1.12, which needs `apache-tvm-ffi<=0.1.11`, and it aborts with `TypeAttr __ffi_repr__ is already registered`. So please don't bump the pins for this sync. Not blocking.

### Coverage

We ran the paths whose FA2 fallback this PR removes, on B300, against the base `28dd9c36`. Accuracy is at base level for softcap, FP8 KV, blocks 16 to 256, mm_prefix, chunked prefill with prefix caching, DCP, windowed encoders (`embeddinggemma-300m`, cosine at least 0.9986 against FA2) and TurboQuant prefill (Qwen3.5-4B). Sinks, the mm encoder and MLA 256/256 have no small hd256 model, so we checked them with direct kernel calls only. DCP improves: on `gemma-2b-it`, TP 2 with DCP 2 scores 0.125 on FA4, against 0.089 on FA2 at the base and 0.125 for TP 2 without DCP.

_This review was prepared with Claude Code and reviewed by a human (@simon-veitner-redhat)._

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

issue_comments.body:
### Blocker: Gemma 4 does not start on Hopper

On one H200, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic` with this PR fails in `kernel_warmup`:

```
File ".../vllm_flash_attn/cute/interface.py", line 823, in _flash_attn_fwd
    validate_output_layout(out, "out", align_bytes=out_align_bytes)
AssertionError: out must have aligned strides and a contiguous last dimension
EngineCore failed to start.
```

FA#213 now requires a 32-byte aligned `out` at `head_dim_v == 512`. `FA4DenseAttentionKernel.get_warmup_keys` compiles SM90 hd512 keys through vLLM's own `compile_flash_attn_varlen_func_from_specs` in `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py`, which builds `out` with the default 16-byte alignment. The FA-side fix does not help, because this wrapper builds its own spec. With only the FA fix, the engine still fails with the same assertion.

The fix is the same line in vLLM's wrapper. It is on [`pr65203-review-fixes`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/tree/pr65203-review-fixes) as one commit, [`fa116c71b`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/fa116c71b2393ee48a4ebc5d0810dfe58a9a1f67), on top of `d203078a1`:

```diff
     out = _make_compile_only_tensor_spec(
         (*q_shape[:-1], v_shape[-1]),
         q_dtype,
+        assumed_align=32 if v_shape[-1] == 512 else 16,
     )
```

On the H200 with this fix, the 5 FA4 warmup keys compile in 10.4 s and GSM8K (5-shot) is 0.6475 flexible / 0.6346 strict. The base (vLLM `28dd9c36`, FA `9ed6b129`) warms up in 14 s and scores 0.6467 / 0.6338.

### Known slowdown: Gemma 2 under forced FLASH_ATTN

Before this PR, hd256 with softcap (Gemma 2, `attn_logit_softcapping=50`) fell back to FA2 on SM100. Now it runs on FA4. Accuracy is unchanged (GSM8K 0.831 against 0.829), but FA4's softcap path is slower. On B300, FLASH_ATTN forced, same server flags, interleaved arms, one GSM8K pass (1319 questions, concurrency 256) takes:

| Arm | Wall time per pass (s) |
|---|---|
| FA4 with softcap (this PR) | 37.8, 37.5, 31.0, 32.9 |
| FA2 (`flash_attn_version=2`) | 21.3, 19.9, 23.5, 20.5 |
| FA4, softcap removed by hf override (timing only) | 12.2, 10.5 |

That is about 1.5x slower than FA2. No FA4 run logged a runtime JIT compile, so this is steady state. Block 128 does not recover it (41.9 s). B300 picks FlashInfer for Gemma 2 by default, so only users who force FLASH_ATTN see this. I am not asking for a change here; it may be worth a line in the description.

### Minor: validation env

The perf numbers reproduce under vLLM's own pins (cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11), which this PR keeps. The env in the description (4.8.1 / 0.1.15.post2) cannot run `vllm serve`: after CUDA-graph capture, the JIT monitor imports tilelang 0.1.12, which needs `apache-tvm-ffi<=0.1.11`, and it aborts with `TypeAttr __ffi_repr__ is already registered`. So please don't bump the pins for this sync. Not blocking.

### Coverage

We ran the paths whose FA2 fallback this PR removes, on B300, against the base `28dd9c36`. Accuracy is at base level for softcap, FP8 KV, blocks 16 to 256, mm_prefix, chunked prefill with prefix caching, DCP, windowed encoders (`embeddinggemma-300m`, cosine at least 0.9986 against FA2) and TurboQuant prefill (Qwen3.5-4B). Sinks, the mm encoder and MLA 256/256 have no small hd256 model, so we checked them with direct kernel calls only. DCP improves: on `gemma-2b-it`, TP 2 with DCP 2 scores 0.125 on FA4, against 0.089 on FA2 at the base and 0.125 for TP 2 without DCP.

_This review was prepared with Claude Code and reviewed by a human (@simon-veitner-redhat)._
